title: 1Password or Bitwarden: Choosing a Password Manager for Home or Business
excerpt: Both are zero-knowledge password managers with AES-256 encryption and independent security audits, so the core security model is close. The differences are in polish, price, openness and how each fits a business identity setup.
verdict: 1Password is the more polished product day to day, and its Secret Key adds a high-entropy second factor on top of the master password when a new device is set up. Bitwarden is open source on both client and server, publishes third-party audit reports, offers a genuinely useful free plan and charges far less for premium features. It can also be self-hosted. For most people the practical security gap is much smaller than the price gap, so let budget, self-hosting needs and how your users feel about the interface decide.
